chunks: Laith al-Murādī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About cushions that are in the house with images on them, on the right or on the left. He said: “There is no harm in it so long as they are not facing the qiblah. And if any part of them is before you, from what is adjacent to the qiblah, then cover it and pray.”

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: images or figurative forms depicted on the cushions
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the house or indoor setting where the prayer takes place
key_terms.الْوَسَائِدِ: cushions or pillows in the house

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in a room with cushions or furnishings that have images on them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning praying in a place where cushions bearing images are present. It indicates that their presence is unobjectionable if they are not positioned facing the qiblah, and if they are directly in front of the worshipper toward the qiblah, they should be covered before salat (prayer).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.740 - Laith al-Muradi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about cushions in the house that have images on them, whether they are to the right or to the left.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it as long as they are not facing the Qibla. If any of them are in front of you, facing the Qibla, then cover them and pray."
